feature1.prompt: This feature aims to enhance the backend processing of Python type hints for UML generation. Currently, the system does not correctly interpret type hints as defined by PEP 484, especially when default values like None are used. The fix should enable the code to accurately extract and process type annotations so that an attribute declared as 'a: str = None' is recognized and its type is correctly determined. After the fix, the underlying type inference and annotation extraction should provide a reliable basis for any further diagram generation.
feature1.hint_texts: Focus on refactoring the type inference and annotation handling logic. This includes updating internal methods that extract type hints from class assignments and managing default values properly. Key areas include ensuring that the new utility functions (for getting annotations and inferring types) correctly process nodes, and that the inspector integrates these functions without losing any existing functionality.
feature1.entrypoint: Modify the following files and functions: in pylint/pyreverse/inspector.py, update the visit_assignname and handle_assignattr_type functions to use the new type inference approach; in pylint/pyreverse/utils.py, implement or update the functions get_annotation_label, get_annotation, and infer_node to properly handle type hints and default None values. This is the starting point for the backend type hint processing enhancements.

feature2.prompt: This feature focuses on enhancing the UML generation process by incorporating Python type hints into the visual output. Currently, UML diagrams generated by the tool do not display type information for class attributes, which diminishes their clarity. The expected behavior is that attributes are shown with their type information (for example, displaying 'a : String' for an attribute defined as 'a: str = None'). The fix should adjust the UML generation to effectively use the backend’s type hint information, resulting in more informative and accurate diagrams.
feature2.hint_texts: Concentrate on revising the UML generation components to utilize the updated type hint information provided by the backend. This involves changes in how nodes are handled in the diagram generation process and updating label creation in the writer module. Emphasis should be placed on ensuring that the type hints are correctly formatted and embedded into the final UML output.
feature2.entrypoint: Modify the following files and functions: in pylint/pyreverse/diagrams.py, adjust the class_names function to correctly process new node types; in pylint/pyreverse/writer.py, update the get_values function to incorporate type hint labels when generating method signatures and attributes. Start by integrating the output from the utility functions so that the diagrams display the expected type information.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features rely on the updated utility module in pylint/pyreverse/utils.py, which provides the type inference and annotation extraction functionality. This shared component is critical for ensuring consistency between the backend processing and the UML generation.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 must expose a robust API for type inference and annotation extraction, which Feature2 will leverage when generating the UML diagrams. It is important that the annotations and types inferred by Feature1 are returned in a format that is easily consumable by the UML generation logic in Feature2.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature1 and Feature2 need to coordinate on the interface of the utility functions and the data structures used to pass type information. Regular discussions and integration meetings should be set up to ensure that both parts are aligned on how type hints are processed and displayed in the output diagrams.
